### Fixed
- `gateway.parameters.dataPlaneResources` is settable through the meta chart (#303). The connectivity chart reads the key (the agentgateway data-plane container's `ephemeral-storage` requests and limits, merged onto the container through `AgentgatewayParameters`) and its schema declares it, but the meta chart's `values.yaml` did not, so the meta chart's generated `values.schema.json` (`gateway.parameters` is `additionalProperties: false`) refused it at render time — `additional properties 'dataPlaneResources' not allowed` — although `forwardAllValues` would have carried it to the connectivity release unchanged; an installation migrating from the standalone chart, whose umbrella accepted the key, hit it. The meta chart now declares the key with the connectivity chart's defaults (`requests.ephemeral-storage: 50Mi`, `limits.ephemeral-storage: 512Mi`), so the rendered platform objects are unchanged until an installation overrides them. `make verify-meta`'s schema-symmetry check compared the two charts' top-level keys only and missed the nested key; it is now `tests/verify-schema-symmetry.py`, which walks the connectivity schema's `properties` (and array `items`) under every block the meta chart forwards and fails on any nested key the meta schema rejects — and the other way round, on any forwarded meta key the connectivity schema does not declare (the roster travels as `components.<name>.enabled` only) — with negative cases proving both directions fail, naming the path. The walk found no other gap.
